text:
anya: Heads up — noticed a flood of reconnects from the EU region starting ~08:10 UTC. Console shows connections healthy but idle_percent spiked to 47% and quotas burned fast.
anya: Most clients are on the WS path, not SSE. Reconnects look like ~every 25-35s.
srini: Did we just flip any keepalive / proxy timeout flags in the canary?
anya: I checked feature flags — streaming_keepalive was toggled to 30s for canary yesterday to reduce idle memory. Changed back at 07:45 but the canary still shows traffic to new route.
julia: Could be proxy -> backend keepalive mismatch. If proxy closes after 30s and client immediately reconnects, we get a reconnect storm and quota churn.
mike: Can you paste a sample conn log?
anya: snippet from router logs:```
2026-03-20T08:11:02Z router[eu-west-1] conn_id=abc123 state=ping_timeout duration=30s closing
2026-03-20T08:11:02Z router[eu-west-1] upstream=ws-pod-9 status=200 bytes=0
2026-03-20T08:11:02Z router[eu-west-1] conn_id=abc123 reconnect true client=mobile-sdk v=1.4.2
```
srini: That looks like a proxy-initiated close (ping timeout). Are our pings forwarded, or does the proxy terminate idle pings?
julia: The envoy config had `connection_idle_timeout: 30s` in canary. Backends expect 65s pings by default. mismatch confirmed.
anya: Console telemetry is tricky here: the health check is hitting the HTTP /health endpoint so it stays green even while streams are being closed. So the rollout dashboard shows healthy.
mike: Oof. So the console rollout UX is misleading — it only reports pod-level health, not stream-level metrics like reconnect_rate, idle_percent, or quota_burn_rate.
srini: For immediate mitigation: revert canary envoy change and bump proxy idle timeout to 70s. Also enable `streaming.preserve_on_grace: true` temporarily to avoid immediate reconnects on close.
julia: Agreed. I'll patch the canary. Deploy command in case anyone needs: `kubectl -n infra set env ds/envoy PROXY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=70s && kubectl rollout restart deployment/envoy-canary`
deploy-bot: deployment/envoy-canary restarted by julia at 08:20 UTC :rocket:
anya: After restart, reconnect rate dropped 10x within 2 mins. Quota burn normalized. But still seeing some edge clients stuck in reconnect loop (old sdk).
mike: Need to add console panel for `streams.connections.reconnect_rate` and alert if > 5/min sustained for 5m. Also surface per-route keepalive vs backend expectation in rollout diffs. UX ticket?
srini: Filed P0 ticket: PLATFORM-STREAM-512. Add to canary checklist: verify stream-level probes and quota smoke test.
julia: Also propose a small change to default server behavior: when we accept a close due to proxy ping timeout, set `Retry-Delay: 250ms` in the close path so clients backoff a bit instead of hammering.
anya: We're also seeing a handful of requests getting `400` on resume attempt after abrupt reconnects (client lib bug). We'll coordinate with SDK team.
mike: For telemetry: tag those reconnect events with `proxy_idle_mismatch=true` so we can filter historical runs. We'll need a short migration to backfill for the last 24h.
anya: TL;DR: root cause = canary envoy idle timeout (30s) mismatched with backend ping (65s) -> proxy closes -> reconnect storms -> quota spike. Fix deployed, monitoring dashboards & rollout UX tasks created. :thumbsup:
srini: Nice triage. Follow-ups: (1) add stream-level readiness probe, (2) surface keepalive config diffs in rollout UI, (3) SDK team to add jittered backoff for reconnects.
julia: I'll add (1) and (2) to sprint. SDK owners pinged.
mike: I'll own the dashboard and alert. Planning to add a temporary console badge when reconnect_rate > threshold so PMs see it during rollouts.
anya: Thanks all. I'll keep an eye for residual reconnects and post updates in #incidents if anything flares up.
ops-bot: Incident check-in: no current pager escalations. Next check at 09:00 UTC.
